extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for CVPR 2024 (assigned referees and Area Chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing CVPR 2024 submissions: how to evaluate technical soundness, novelty, ethics, conflicts, use of supplementary/rebuttal, and acceptable reviewer behavior. Targets assigned reviewers and Area Chairs handling reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance standard: technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for what is good or stimulating in the paper, and what knowledge advancement it has made. Embrace novel, brave concepts, even if not tested on many datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh novelty and potential impact alongside reported performance
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to weigh both the novelty and potential impact of the work alongside the reported performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not exceeding state-of-the-art on an existing benchmark is not grounds for rejection by itself; evaluate novelty and potential impact as part of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor correctable flaws should not cause rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor flaws that can be easily corrected should not be a reason to reject a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If problems are fixable in revision (e.g., clarity, small missing experiments), these alone should not justify rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and detailed in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your discussion, more than your score, will help authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific feedback on ways authors can improve their papers. Short reviews are unhelpful; bullet lists with one short sentence per bullet are NOT a detailed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check assignments for conflicts and comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you get your reviewing assignment, ensure you have no obvious conflict of interest and you feel comfortable reviewing the paper assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues arise, contact the Area Chair immediately as instructed in assignment emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and follow Author Guidelines and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Author Guidelines carefully to familiarize yourself with all official policies the authors are expected to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe a paper may violate a policy, contact the Chairs; otherwise proceed assuming no violation. Consult Ethics Guidelines and Suggested Practices for Authors for specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect anonymity in the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not take active steps to discover the identity of the authors, and make all efforts to keep their own identity invisible to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to find author identities by searching the web. Knowing authors from arXiv is not itself a violation; treat papers fairly whether or not you know the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ideas and maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the confidentiality of the ideas represented in the papers you review; CVPR submissions are not published documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show the paper or supplementary material to anyone (except those you explicitly ask to help with your review). Do not use ideas/code from papers you review. After the review process, destroy copies of papers, supplementary material, and any implementations or results produced while reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be absolutely no question about the impartiality of any review; return the paper if your review would create a possible conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COIs include (but are not limited to): same institution as an author; direct involvement in the work; perceived conflicts; collaboration in past three years (e.g., coauthored papers or grants); being an MS/PhD advisor or advisee (treat carefully, often considered lifetime COI). Contact the Area Chair if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and constructive in tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful review; belittling or sarcastic comments have no place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid second-person addressing of authors ('you') and avoid referring to the authors at all if possible; prefer referring to 'the paper'. Word critiques constructively while remaining honest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take time to form and write your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally, read a paper and think about it over the course of several days before you write your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time to write thoughtful and detailed reviews rather than brief or rushed comments; detailed reasoning helps ACs and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about writing clarity and how to improve it
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suggest the writing needs to be improved, point to particular sections and give suggestions for how they can be clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite exact sections or paragraphs that are unclear and propose concrete revisions or restructuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and evidentiary about novelty/prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that the submitted work 'has been done before' MUST be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For positive reviews, summarize the novel aspects in the Strengths section. If you suspect plagiarism or dishonesty, bring concerns to the Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle arXiv prior art and missing comparisons appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to thoroughly compare to recent arXiv reports; failing to cite arXiv or failing to beat its performance SHOULD NOT be SOLE grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should acknowledge directly relevant arXiv work; reviewers may suggest acknowledging or being aware of arXiv work but should not demand exhaustive comparisons or reject solely for arXiv issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not request authors to cite your own work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not give away your identity by asking the authors to cite several of your own papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid self-promotion requests in review text; use objective citation requests when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: If out of scope, explain and suggest alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If you think the paper is out of scope for CVPR's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review and suggest other publication possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless mismatch is extreme, keep an open mind because the conference seeks a diverse set of good papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be generous with suggestions for future work or improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Give authors new ideas for how they can improve their work (new tools, datasets, application areas, or ways to generalize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete suggestions increase a paper's chances of improvement and help authors focus revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material: consult only as needed and watch for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is intended to provide details of derivations and results that do not fit within the paper format or space limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper should indicate when to consult supplementary. Supplementary MAY NOT include results obtained with an improved version of the method or updated/corrected PDFs. If you find violations, contact the Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal policy: no requests for substantial additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not request substantial additional experiments for the rebuttal, or penalize for lack of additional experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial refers to what would be needed in a major revision. You may request clarifications or additional illustrations in the rebuttal. Rebuttal may include illustrative figures or comparison tables; do not penalize papers for including extra results, but you can ignore them when deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media disclosures by others are not automatic violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a social media post shared information on a CVPR submission without the authors being involved, this is not a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A violation occurs only when authors proactively share the submission; treat such disclosures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn datasets require close scrutiny but are not automatic disqualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a withdrawn dataset (e.g., DukeMTMC-ReID) is not in itself grounds for rejection, but should invite very close scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag such cases in the review form for AC/PC consideration. Consider whether authors explain why they used the dataset and whether acceptable alternatives exist. If paper could be accepted without the withdrawn-dataset experiments, advise removal of those experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers must not require authors to evaluate on withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation of policy for a reviewer or Area Chair to require comparison on a dataset that has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ask authors to run experiments on withdrawn datasets; flag concerns for AC consideration instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating dataset-as-contribution claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission claims a dataset as one of its contributions, there should be a reasonable expectation that the dataset will be made publicly available upon publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private or restricted datasets need not result in rejection, but they cannot be claimed as contributions in their own right. Judge the paper by its other technical merits if datasets are private.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM usage policy for referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees may use any device, including an LLM, to polish their review wording, but must vouch for and be responsible for the accuracy of the review. It is misconduct to allow an LLM to see a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polishing a summary with an LLM that hasn't seen the paper is acceptable if the reviewer vouches for it. Providing the submission to an LLM (so the LLM has seen the paper) is a serious violation that may lead to exclusion from submitting to CVPR for up to two years. Authors can complain to ACs with supporting examples; PCs may act on complaints.
